en: During a thunderstorm, avoid standing under tall trees because lightning is more likely to strike the highest object.
If an earthquake happens indoors, drop to the floor, take cover under a sturdy desk, and hold on tightly.
Because the water cycle moves pollutants into rivers, you must always boil floodwater for one minute before drinking it to kill bacteria.
Drinking plenty of water during the dry season prevents heatstroke, which occurs when your body overheats from extreme sun exposure.
Washing vegetables thoroughly removes harmful soil-borne parasites like roundworm eggs that can cause severe stomach infections if accidentally ingested.
Avoid playing near steep cliffs made of loose shale because heavy rain can easily trigger dangerous, falling rock fragments.
Earth's atmosphere blocks most harmful solar radiation, but you still need sunscreen to protect your skin from the Sun's ultraviolet rays.
During a typhoon, evacuate to higher ground immediately if authorities warn of a storm surge to avoid drowning in seawater.
The Moon's gravity causes spring tides during full moons, creating unusually high water levels that can sweep swimmers away from beaches.
The bright star Sirius helps sailors navigate the open ocean at night, proving that understanding stars can keep you safe from getting lost.
Never cross a swollen river during the rainy season because fast-moving flash floods can easily sweep a person off their feet.
Emptying stagnant water from old tires prevents mosquitoes from breeding, which stops the spread of dengue fever during the wet season.
